summary.en-US: Connect OpenCode, Codex and MCP agents to your browser for page search, forms, screenshots and local action memory.

version.approval_notes: Source is supplied. Build with Bun 1.3.6: bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && bun run build:extension:firefox. Native messaging relays explicitly requested browser data to a locally installed host and connected agents. Cloud decision assistance is off by default; screenshot sharing is separately opt-in. Firefox automation uses a user-configured loopback WebDriver BiDi endpoint. No remote executable code or telemetry.

description.en-US:
OpenCode Browser connects your coding agent to a browser profile you choose. It works with OpenCode, Codex, Claude and other MCP clients through the opencode-chromium package.

Use it to:
• Search and inspect pages without copying everything into a chat.
• Navigate tabs, fill forms, use the keyboard and take screenshots.
• Keep separate agent sessions organized in named browser profiles.
• Review upload requests before files are sent to a website.
• Save successful actions in optional local memory for repeat tasks.

The panel brings connection status, decision assistance and memory into three views: Overview, Profiles and Settings. Detailed usage and diagnostics expand when you need them. Light and dark themes follow your system.

Optional decision assistance can rank ambiguous targets with Jev through OpenRouter or TypeSafe, or OpenAI Luna through OpenRouter. Cloud assistance is off by default. Luna screenshot sharing needs a separate opt-in. These services require your own API key and may charge for use.

Getting started:
1. Install the extension.
2. Run: npx -y opencode-chromium@latest setup --all
3. Restart your coding agent and choose the browser profile shown in the extension.

The extension requires the local native host installed by that command. It is a browser automation bridge, not a standalone chatbot. Requested page content and screenshots go to the agent you connect, which may send them to its model provider. Saved action memory stays on your device. Upload confirmation is on by default; turning it off allows uploads without a prompt. The extension has no telemetry.

Chromium browsers use the browser's debugger extension API. Firefox and LibreWolf also require the Remote Agent to be enabled at launch and configured on loopback. Setup instructions and troubleshooting: https://github.com/Quindart-com/opencode-chromium

Open source under the MIT license.

privacy_policy.en-US: Requested browser content, URLs, screenshots and actions are relayed to your local native host and the agent you connect. That agent may send tool outputs to its model provider. Action memory stays on your device. Optional decision assistance sends bounded intent and candidate descriptions to your chosen provider only after you enable it. Luna screenshots require a separate opt-in. Upload confirmation is on by default and can be disabled in Settings. This extension has no telemetry and does not independently monitor browsing. You can disable assistance, revoke screenshot sharing and remove saved provider keys in Settings.
